npcs.name: Mayor Haldrin Moth
npcs.description: Town Mayor associated with the council chamber and festival platforms.
npcs.biography: Ask around town for a town mayor and someone will point you to Mayor at the council chamber and festival platforms. At 59, this Human has learned which smiles are currency and which are warnings. Mayor clears his throat before every compromise, and is rarely without chain of office that pinches when he lies. Patronized by Edric; depends on Penna; peers with Sava. What drives them is simple to name and hard to finish: they want to leave town richer in goodwill than coin. What keeps them careful is a scandal collapsing Midsummer trade. To a DM, Mayor is ready to roleplay immediately—useful for favors, local color, or trouble. Accepted Edric's festival funding with fewer questions than Penna liked.
npcs.personality: clears his throat before every compromise. Professional demeanor of a seasoned town mayor.
npcs.motivation: Pursue this: leave town richer in goodwill than coin. Avoid this: a scandal collapsing Midsummer trade.
npcs.secret: Privately terrified of a scandal collapsing Midsummer trade, and currently entangled with: Accepted Edric's festival funding with fewer questions than Penna liked.
npcs.rumor: Rumor says Mayor can tell you anything that happens near the council chamber and festival platforms—for a price or a kindness.
npcs.voice: Speaks like a Human town mayor: concrete details first, embellishment only when useful.
npcs.appearance: Human; often near the council chamber and festival platforms; look for chain of office that pinches when he lies.

npcs.name: Penna Ledgerwell
npcs.description: Town Clerk associated with the records hall.
npcs.biography: Penna Ledgerwell works as a town clerk out of the records hall, a 32-year-old Human with more town memory than most council minutes. Penna alphabetizes emergencies, and is rarely without ribbon tags for 'urgent', 'political', and 'do not lose'. Essential to Mayor; threat to Orin; overflow to Hala. What drives them is simple to name and hard to finish: they want to digitize nothing and perfect everything on paper. What keeps them careful is forged seals passing her desk. To a DM, Penna is ready to roleplay immediately—useful for favors, local color, or trouble. Flagged a warehouse writ with Pale Orin's distinctive pen pressure.

npcs.name: Bailiff Crowe
npcs.description: Bailiff associated with collection rounds and holding cells.
npcs.biography: Most days begin the same for Bailiff Crowe: a 48-year-old Human bailiff moving through collection rounds and holding cells as if the stones themselves keep appointments with them. Bailiff recites fine schedules like scripture, and is rarely without baton he has never raised and always shows. Works with Judge Sava; pressured by alleys. What drives them is simple to name and hard to finish: they want to enforce law without starring in Kitty's rumors. What keeps them careful is becoming Marrow's public face. To a DM, Bailiff is ready to roleplay immediately—useful for favors, local color, or trouble. Was offered a bribe to 'misplace' Rook's holding paperwork.

npcs.name: Miln Tallcount
npcs.description: Tax Assessor associated with doorsteps with a counting board.
npcs.biography: Most days begin the same for Miln Tallcount: a 53-year-old Halfling tax assessor moving through doorsteps with a counting board as if the stones themselves keep appointments with them. Miln apologizes and assesses in the same breath, and is rarely without folding abacus and a rainproof satchel. Unpopular; useful against Nedda; supports Bera. What drives them is simple to name and hard to finish: they want to fund Bera's second well through honest tallies. What keeps them careful is being drowned in a well 'accident' of popularity. To a DM, Miln is ready to roleplay immediately—useful for favors, local color, or trouble. Found undeclared barge income patterns matching Nedda's trips.

npcs.name: Judge Sava Wren
npcs.description: Magistrate associated with the magistrate's bench.
npcs.biography: Judge Sava Wren works as a magistrate out of the magistrate's bench, a 61-year-old Half-Elf with more town memory than most council minutes. Judge makes eye contact with the poorest person first, and is rarely without gavel with a softened rim. Peer to Mayor; works with Crowe and Merrick. What drives them is simple to name and hard to finish: they want to set a precedent that ledgers bind lords too. What keeps them careful is nobles buying outcomes through festival gifts. To a DM, Judge is ready to roleplay immediately—useful for favors, local color, or trouble. Asked Merrick for a clean chain of evidence on Rook before festival court.

npcs.name: Bol Brightvoice
npcs.description: Town Herald associated with corners, steps, and market cries.
npcs.biography: Bol Brightvoice works as a town herald out of corners, steps, and market cries, a 28-year-old Human with more town memory than most council minutes. Bol projects news until windows open, and is rarely without brass bell with a cracked throat. Voice of government; confused by mill intrigue. What drives them is simple to name and hard to finish: they want to be trusted with truth, not only volume. What keeps them careful is reading a proclamation that starts a riot. To a DM, Bol is ready to roleplay immediately—useful for favors, local color, or trouble. Was handed two conflicting proclamations about mill ownership in one morning.
